title: Langroid SQLChatAgent -- T1059 LLM-generated SQL COPY-FROM-PROGRAM RCE via prompt injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-25879 (GHSA-mxfr-6hcw-j9rq,
CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for Langroid, a framework
for building LLM-powered applications.

Prior to 0.63.0, `SQLChatAgent` executed SQL produced by an LLM
(`run_query()`, `sql_chat_agent.py:474`) with no sanitization or
validation of what the model chose to emit. Because an LLM's output is
influenceable by prompt injection -- including INDIRECTLY, via data the
agent reads back from elsewhere -- an attacker who can shape any input
the agent later processes can coerce it into emitting a
`RunQueryTool` call carrying a dialect-specific dangerous primitive
rather than a plain query. When the configured database role holds
execute-adjacent privileges (`pg_execute_server_program` on Postgres,
`FILE` on MySQL, `xp_cmdshell` on MSSQL), this reaches full RCE on the
database host -- the advisory's own example is PostgreSQL's
`COPY log(content) FROM PROGRAM 'id';`. This is command execution
reached through a SQL interface, not a credential-theft primitive, so it
is filed under `execution` (T1059, command and scripting interpreter)
rather than `credential_access`.

Detection logic flags exactly the primitive that turns "the LLM ran a
query" into "the LLM ran a command": a `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM`
(Postgres), `LOAD_FILE`/`INTO OUTFILE` (MySQL), or `xp_cmdshell`
(MSSQL) statement appearing in database query-log content -- these
primitives have no reason to originate from a normal chat-agent query
workload, regardless of which application layer emitted them.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (langroid, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.63.0 (SELECT-only sqlglot-parsed allowlist
with a dialect-aware dangerous-pattern blocklist;
`allow_dangerous_operations=True` restores the old behavior for
deployments that accept the risk deliberately).
